EgressPolicyActionType.description: Types of actions that an egress policy rule can take.

EgressPolicyHeaderTransform.description: Describes a header transformation to apply to matching requests.

EgressPolicyHookFailBehavior.description: What the egress proxy should do when a webhook invocation fails (timeout, non-2xx, invalid payload, SSRF-rejected URL, etc.).

EgressPolicyHookRef.description: Configures a webhook called at request time for rules whose static decision cannot be expressed declaratively. When a rule's EgressPolicyHookRef? EgressPolicyRule.HookRef is set, the egress proxy POSTs a request-context payload to string EgressPolicyHookRef.Endpoint and applies the returned decision (Allow / Deny / Transform / Rewrite) in place of the rule's static Action.  EgressRuleRoutingMode EgressPolicyHookRef.RoutingMode controls how the egress proxy reaches the webhook endpoint itself: EgressRuleRoutingMode.Vnet binds the outbound socket to the sandbox's customer VNET IP (so the hook host can be a private service reachable only from inside the VNET), EgressRuleRoutingMode.Platform forces the node's platform egress, and EgressRuleRoutingMode.Default uses the sandbox-level routing. The webhook response itself can also carry a `routingMode` field that overrides routing for the downstream upstream call when the decision is Rewrite.

EgressPolicyManagedIdentityRef.description: References a managed identity token to be fetched and injected as a header value. EgressPolicyManagedIdentityType? EgressPolicyManagedIdentityRef.Type must be set to specify which identity to use.

EgressPolicyRule.description: A single egress policy rule. Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins. A rule has either a static EgressPolicyRuleAction? EgressPolicyRule.Action or a dynamic EgressPolicyHookRef? EgressPolicyRule.HookRef, never both. When EgressPolicyHookRef? EgressPolicyRule.HookRef is set, the proxy calls the configured webhook at request time and applies the returned decision in place of EgressPolicyRuleAction? EgressPolicyRule.Action.

EgressPolicyRuleAction.description: The action to take when a rule matches. For Rewrite actions, Scheme/Host/Path specify the destination to rewrite the request to, and EgressRuleRoutingMode EgressPolicyRuleAction.RoutingMode optionally overrides the sandbox-level egress routing for this rule.

forward.description: Controls how matching traffic is forwarded.

forwardProxy.description: The proxy used to forward matching traffic.

EgressPolicyRuleMatch.description: Request matching criteria for an egress policy rule. All specified conditions must match (AND logic). EgressPolicyMatchScheme? EgressPolicyRuleMatch.Scheme is nullable; null means the author did not specify a scheme and the effective default is resolved per rule polarity at evaluation time. A static Deny defaults to EgressPolicyMatchScheme.Any so a block is not silently scoped to HTTPS and bypassed over HTTP. Every other rule — including positive rules (Allow / Transform / Rewrite) and dynamic EgressPolicyHookRef? EgressPolicyRule.HookRef rules (whose outcome can be Allow/Transform/Rewrite or fail open) — defaults to EgressPolicyMatchScheme.Https: on plaintext HTTP there is no SNI, so matching uses the sandbox-controlled Host header with no certificate validation, and a positive or hook match there would let a sandbox reach a non-allowlisted IP while spoofing an allowlisted Host. Set EgressPolicyMatchScheme.Any explicitly to match both schemes, or EgressPolicyMatchScheme.Http / EgressPolicyMatchScheme.Https to pin a single scheme. For IP-based match hosts, scheme matching is ignored (no TLS certificate validation applies to IPs anyway).bool? EgressPolicyRuleMatch.NormalizePath controls whether the request path is decoded and normalized (encoded-slash decode, slash merging, and ./.. dot-segment removal) before it is matched against string? EgressPolicyRuleMatch.Path. It defaults to enabled (null is treated as true) to prevent path-confusion bypasses where an encoded path such as /allowed%2F.. matches an allow rule but the upstream server resolves it to a different path. Set to false only for upstreams that require the raw, un-normalized path.

environment.description: Optional environment variables to set in the sandbox container. These variables will override any environment variables with the same key from the image. Cannot be specified when creating from a snapshot. The combined UTF-8 size of the environment entries in KEY=VALUE format must not exceed 1.75 MiB. Entries above the Linux 128 KiB per-entry limit are logged for compatibility monitoring.

connections.description: Optional list of connection IDs to associate with the sandbox (1P flow).

gatewayConnections.description: Optional list of AI Gateway connections for 3P sandbox creation. Each entry contains the MCP server config resource ID, MCP runtime URL, and identity configuration. Mutually exclusive with IReadOnlyList<ConnectionId>? SandboxRequest.Connections — do not provide both. Maximum of 10 entries.

credentialRefs.description: Optional list of sandbox-group credential names to associate with the sandbox. Each name must reference a credential configured on the parent sandbox group.

ports.description: Optional list of ports to expose on the sandbox during creation.

egressPolicyId.description: Optional reference to a named egress policy. When specified, the named policy's rules are resolved and merged with any inline rules (inline rules take precedence). The named policy must exist in the sandbox's sandbox group.

anthropicApiKey.description: Optional Anthropic API key for Claude preset. Only used when presetSandboxType is Claude.

identitySettings.description: Optional identity settings that control which managed identities from the group are available to this sandbox and in which lifecycle phases. When null or empty, the default delegation behavior applies (delegated-only when any delegated identity exists).

volumes.description: Optional list of volumes to mount in the sandbox. When SandboxSource? SandboxRequest.SourcesRef.Snapshot is set, the listed volumes are attached after the sandbox is restored from the snapshot — semantically equivalent to restoring the sandbox first and then calling the dynamic add-volume-mount API. In that mode the volumes must all be data disks, the snapshot must be non-pod, and the snapshot must not already have its own attached volumes; cluster placement is constrained to a cluster that already holds the referenced data disks (cross-cluster download is not supported). Those rules are enforced downstream after the snapshot/volume Cosmos lookups.

contentPackageDownloads.description: Optional list of content packages to download onto the sandbox during creation. Each entry specifies a content package ID and target path where it will be downloaded.

vnetConnectionName.description: Optional vnet connection name to use for VNET injection. When specified, the sandbox traffic will be routed through the VNET identified by this connection. Requires the sandbox to be created within an ARM-managed sandbox group that has the named vnet connection.

systemVnetConnectionName.description: Optional system vnet connection name for system-managed VNET injection. Works identically to string? SandboxRequest.VnetConnectionName but references a system VNet connection.

isDelegationBackingResource.description: Indicates this sandbox is created within a sandbox group that has resource delegations. Resolved from the sandbox group at the controller level and forwarded to the cluster so the Identity Proxy can suppress non-delegated identities even when no delegated identities exist yet.

TdsAuthKind.description: Credential kind for a TDS egress connection. Managed identity is deferred (v1).

TdsCredential.description: A declared TDS credential. string TdsCredential.Name uniquely identifies the credential within its TdsEgressSection and is what rules (string? TdsEgressAction.Credential) and webhook responses reference. On the API/contract path EgressPolicySecretRef? TdsCredential.SecretRef is set and string? TdsCredential.Secret is null. On the runtime path (after Global API resolution) string? TdsCredential.Secret holds the resolved material and flows (encrypted) to NodeAgent.

TdsEgressAction.description: Static action for a TDS rule. EgressPolicyActionType TdsEgressAction.Type must be Allow or Deny (Transform/Rewrite are HTTP-only and rejected by validation). string? TdsEgressAction.Credential names a declared credential and is only valid on Allow.

TdsEgressMatch.description: Match criteria for a TDS egress rule (AND logic). Host is a glob over the SNI / original-dst server.

TdsEgressRule.description: A single TDS egress rule. Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins. A rule has exactly one of TdsEgressAction? TdsEgressRule.Action (static) or EgressPolicyHookRef? TdsEgressRule.HookRef (dynamic webhook), never both — same XOR as HTTP.

TdsEgressSection.description: The TDS section of an egress policy. IReadOnlyList<TdsCredential> TdsEgressSection.Credentials is a list of named credentials (each string TdsCredential.Name unique within the section), declared once and referenced by name from static rules and webhook responses. The array-of-named-objects shape matches the rest of the ADC API (for example Connections); the runtime resolves it into a by-name map. On the runtime path each credential's string? TdsCredential.Secret is resolved.

TransportEgressSection.description: The transport (L3/L4 TCP/UDP) section of an egress policy. Distinct from HTTP and TDS policy and enforced by NodeAgent at the network layer (`iptables`). EgressPolicyActionType TransportEgressSection.DefaultAction is the terminal action applied to raw TCP/UDP flows that match no rule; IReadOnlyList<TransportEgressRule> TransportEgressSection.Rules is capped at 10 entries. DNS (port 53) is always carved out and never constrained by these rules in v1.

TransportProtocol.description: L4 transport protocol for an L3 egress rule.
